run.question:
We have an active P1 incident — the checkout service in our production-us-east-2
cluster is throwing 500 errors and customers cannot complete payments. This
started in the last few hours. Please investigate the root cause using the
app-259-prod-logs index.

report.summary: No data for the cluster named in the request exists in what this Run can read. The log index the request points at, app-259-prod-logs, holds 9 documents inside the authorized window 2026-11-20T05:41:29Z–2026-11-21T05:41:29Z, and every one of them carries cluster=production-eu-west-2 and region=eu-west-2; none carries production-us-east-2. Those eu-west-2 records do describe checkout/payment failures (payment-provider timeouts, 502/504 answers, a checkout circuit breaker opening for payment-service at a 38% failure rate), but they belong to a different cluster and are not evidence about the production-us-east-2 incident, so no root cause is named. The only Kubernetes cluster this Run can read is production-eu-west-2 (namespaces otel-demo and app-100a); there, checkout and payment deployments are 1/1 ready, all otel-demo pods are Running and ready, and sampled checkout and payment container logs between 04:41Z and 05:40Z show completed payments, so that cluster is not shown as broken by the evidence looked at. Prometheus and Jaeger returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE for every query attempted, so no metric or trace signal could be checked for either cluster. Overall: the reported production-us-east-2 checkout 500s are unverified and unexplainable from the evidence available, and the diagnosis has to wait for data from that cluster.

claims.text: The only Elasticsearch index available in this Run is app-259-prod-logs (9 documents, 9.6kb, green); a wildcard index listing of '*' returned no other index.

All 9 documents in app-259-prod-logs inside the authorized window carry cluster=production-eu-west-2 (9/9) and region=eu-west-2 (9/9); the term aggregations over cluster and region returned only those buckets, with 0 documents in other buckets. No document of this index in this window carries cluster=production-us-east-2.

The eu-west-2 (production-eu-west-2) documents in app-259-prod-logs show, in time order: 2026-11-21T02:41:19Z checkout-service WARN 'Latency on POST /api/checkout p95=1800ms (target 800ms)'; 03:41:19Z checkout-service ERROR 500 'payment provider response timeout after 30s' and payment-service ERROR 504 'Upstream timeout calling provider /v68/payments after 30000ms' for correlation_id chk-eu-1142; 04:41:19Z two checkout-service ERROR 500 'circuit-breaker open for payment-service (failure rate 38% > 25% threshold)' (chk-eu-1208, chk-eu-1209); 04:56:19Z payment-service ERROR 504 same upstream timeout; 05:11:19Z checkout-service ERROR 500 'payment provider returned 502 Bad Gateway'; 05:26:19Z payment-service WARN 'Payment provider degraded mode acknowledged via status page; retry queue depth=842'; 05:36:19Z checkout-service INFO 'Recovery: circuit-breaker half-open, success rate 92% over last 60s'. Aggregated levels: 6 ERROR, 2 WARN, 1 INFO; status codes 4x500, 3x200, 2x504.

In the cluster this Run can read (production-eu-west-2), Deployment checkout and Deployment payment in namespace otel-demo each show replicas=1, ready=1, available=1, updated=1; all 22 otel-demo pods are phase Running with ready=true, and the checkout pod checkout-6578865d87-5zx6n (restartCount 1, lastState Unknown) shows no error-class lines other than two info lines ('payment went through (transaction_id: ...)' at 04:54:41Z and 'order confirmation email sent' at 05:34:34Z) among 291 lines read, while the payment pod payment-6f7bc865d6-9z92d logged 'Transaction complete.' for charges at 04:41:46Z, 05:08:44Z, 05:09:42Z, 05:16:04Z, 05:24:40Z and 05:31:14Z. That cluster's sampled evidence therefore does not show an active checkout/payment failure between 04:41Z and 05:40Z, although probe of a sample is not a failure-rate measurement.

Kubernetes events in the accessible production-eu-west-2 cluster for the window show two scale-up rollouts at 05:38Z: Deployment/loki in app-100a scaled replica set loki-66445c6d6f from 0 to 1 (SuccessfulCreate, Pod Scheduled/Pulled/Created/Started for pod loki-66445c6d6f-27wwv), and Deployment/payment-api-100a in app-100a scaled replica set payment-api-100a-64dcc58445 from 0 to 1 (pod payment-api-100a-64dcc58445-6w458, image python:3.9-slim); also one Warning event at 2026-11-21T05:28:04Z on Endpoints/loki in namespace default, reason FailedToCreateEndpoint, message 'Failed to create endpoint for service app-282/loki: endpoints "loki" already exists'. These are eu-west-2 objects and were not tied to any production-us-east-2 evidence.

Hypothesis, unverified for the named cluster: the production-us-east-2 checkout 500s may be the same failure class visible in the production-eu-west-2 log records, i.e. checkout-service returning 500 because its payment dependency times out or answers 502/504 badly enough to open a circuit breaker. Support would require the us-east-2 pod logs, payment-service error spans or rpc error metrics for the incident window; none of those were obtained.

Rejected as this incident's evidence: the checkout/payment error records in app-259-prod-logs are all labelled cluster=production-eu-west-2, region=eu-west-2, so they cannot be used to explain or locate a fault in production-us-east-2; the egress/rollout activity at 05:38Z in app-100a (loki, payment-api-100a) is also in the eu-west-2 cluster and no evidence ties it to checkout in either region.

Get data from production-us-east-2 itself: point the log pipeline or an index at that cluster (the only index here, app-259-prod-logs, carries only production-eu-west-2), then read checkout-service and payment-service error lines, pod status/last termination reason and events for that cluster in the incident window.

Once Prometheus and Jaeger are reachable again, compare checkout error rate (traces_span_metrics_calls_total status_code), payment rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_count/rpc_server_duration_milliseconds_bucket by rpc_grpc_status_code, and app_payment_transactions_total in production-us-east-2 against a pre-incident baseline before drawing any latency or error-rate conclusion.

gaps: No data for cluster production-us-east-2 was found: app-259-prod-logs is the only index present and all 9 of its documents (2026-11-21T02:41:19Z–05:36:19Z) are cluster=production-eu-west-2 / region=eu-west-2. The production-us-east-2 checkout 500s are therefore unverified, as is whether any us-east-2 service is affected.

Prometheus was unreachable in this Run: get_all_labels, get_label_values (service_name, and with match traces_span_metrics_calls_total), get_metric_names, and execute_prometheus_instant_query (query 'up') each returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so no metric series (including cluster or region labels) could be read for any cluster.

Jaeger was unreachable in this Run: traces_list_services and traces_search (service checkout) each returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so no span, error status tag or call edge could be inspected for any cluster.

Kubernetes access is limited to the production-eu-west-2 cluster; no production-us-east-2 Kubernetes object (deployment, pod, event, networkpolicy, service) could be read, so pod status, termination reasons, events and application logs for the named cluster remain unknown.
The change_history integration is not available, so no deployment, config or provider-side change record could be checked for either cluster or for the payment provider dependency.

The app-259-prod-logs documents name an external payment provider path (/v68/payments) but its identity, status page and its own telemetry were not available; the 'degraded mode acknowledged via status page' WARN cannot be independently verified.

Whether the 500s the request reports are the same signals as the eu-west-2 log records is unknown; the eu-west-2 cluster check (deployments 1/1 ready, pods running, sample logs showing completed payments) neither confirms nor rules out a production-us-east-2 fault.

Kubernetes events in production-eu-west-2 include scale-ups of Deployment/loki and Deployment/payment-api-100a in app-100a at 05:38Z and a Warning FailedToCreateEndpoint on Endpoints/loki at 05:28:04Z; they are in a different cluster from the incident and could not be placed as affected or as changed for a stated other reason relevant to this incident.
next_steps: Confirm with the incident owner the exact cluster/region identifier and the first observed 500 timestamp for the production-us-east-2 checkout service.
Ship or point a log index (and metric/trace source) at production-us-east-2, then re-run the checkout/payment error and pod-status checks there.
Once metrics are reachable, compare production-us-east-2 checkout error rate and payment call latency against a pre-incident baseline of the same length, and record the sampled times used.

Ask the payment provider team for the /v68/payments provider status and error ratio in the incident window, since upstream timeouts and 502/504 answers are the failure pattern seen in the analogous eu-west-2 records.
